thread:
Aisha (People Ops): Quick question 1 office was closed for unexpected plumbing repairs for 8 business days last month. Some people worked remotely, a few logged vacation, and a couple had partial unpaid LOAs. Do accruals/quarter cutoffs need special handling? @Jon (Payroll) any immediate guidance? cc @Lena (HRBP)

Jon (Payroll): Accruals follow paid status for the pay period. If payroll shows them as paid (regular pay) then accruals should be unchanged. Unpaid LOAs will reduce accruals. I'll run a reconciliation and flag exceptions.

Megan (People Ops): Important: were employees marked under a company-paid closure code or treated as regular remote work? That determines messaging and whether we offer any goodwill carryover.

Aisha (People Ops): Default was remote work allowed; ops administratively recorded the building as closed. A handful logged PTO instead of remote. I'll pull the attendance export.

Carlos (Eng Manager): For my team everyone logged normal hours except one FTE who took 3 days PTO and one contractor who took a week unpaid. Contractors shouldn't accrue, right?

Jon (Payroll): Contractors per our policy don't accrue PTO. For FTEs, if pay records show paid hours or salary for the pay period, accrual should apply. I'll run: SELECT emp_id, pay_code, pay_amount FROM payroll WHERE period_start >= '2026-04-01' AND period_end <= '2026-04-15'; and compare to accrual logs.

Lena (HRBP): If any paid employees missed accruals due to a system flag bug, we'll do retro adjustments. Also consider a one-time carryover exception if someone had to cancel planned leave because of the closure.

Aisha (People Ops): Agreed. Need the reconciled list before the payroll cutoff tomorrow 3pm PT. @Jon can you confirm ETA?

Jon (Payroll): ETA 90 minutes. I'll post a spreadsheet in #people-ops-shared with columns: emp_id, fte_status, expected_accrual, actual_accrual, discrepancy_reason.

hr-bot: FYI: PTO policy v2.1 states accruals are computed on paid status by pay period. See internal doc: https://redwood.internal/hr/pto-policy

Megan (People Ops): I'll draft comms for affected employees: what we're fixing, that no action is needed, and any manual adjustments will reflect on the next payroll statement.

Jon (Payroll): Uploaded: office-plumbing-accruals-1743200001.xlsx 1 flagged 5 FTE rows for manual retro accruals (system flagged them as unpaid due to a badge-yesterday sync bug). I'll coordinate GL entries with finance.

Carlos (Eng Manager): Thanks. For future outages could we have an "office-closure" payroll flag to auto-handle accrual and message templates? Reduces tickets.

Lena (HRBP): Good suggestion. I'll add an FAQ entry and policy language update, and Megan can add templates to the comms library.

Aisha (People Ops): Closing loop: Megan will send comms, Jon will post when journal entries are scheduled, Lena will update policy docs. If any employee reaches out, ask them to wait for the official note.

Megan (People Ops): Draft ready. Will post in the shared doc and queue to send after retro entries are confirmed.

Jon (Payroll): Journal entries scheduled for next AP run. Spreadsheet link and notes in #people-ops-shared.

Aisha (People Ops): Thanks team. :thumbsup:
